## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Mālutajātaka* (Ja 17) is a short canonical birth story preserved in the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. In the edition of the Jātaka commentary by V. Fausböll, the text opens with the verse pratīka *Kāle va yadi va junhe ti* (“In light or dark”) [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral]. According to the introductory narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha recounted the story while staying at Jetavana regarding two monks who had gone forth into the monastic order in their old age [Fausböll 1877; SuttaCentral]. Living together in a forest hermitage in the Kosala country, the two elders—designated as Elder Dark (*Kāla*) and Elder Light (*Juṇha*)—fell into a dispute regarding when cold weather occurs, one contending that cold appears during the dark fortnight and the other insisting that it appears during the bright fortnight of the month [SuttaCentral].

Neither SuttaCentral nor computational scans in DharmaNexus register any Pali-internal text reuse or cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan Buddhist literature [DharmaNexus; SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records seven modern translations across five languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato under the title *The Breeze* [SuttaCentral].
